title: In Silico Molecular Modeling of the Sodium Iodide Symporter from Homo sapiens
author: Hristina R. Zhekova
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bb46iqze
materials: Hristina R. Zhekova and Sergei Y. Noskov
3D threading and refinement of the models

steps.title: Prepare NIS sequence alignments
steps.instruction: Align the human NIS sequence with six LeuT‑fold templates (LeuT, AdiC, BetP, dDAT, Mhp1, vSGLT) using the Modeller 9.187 align tool, remove the putative TM 1, 12 and 13 regions, and align the remaining residues 50‑439 (5+5 fold) to the templates; model TM 1 and TM 12 after vSGLT (PDB 2XQ2 and 3DH4) and exclude TM 13 from modeling due to low identity.

substeps.instruction: Identify the six LeuT‑fold templates: LeuT, AdiC, BetP, dDAT, Mhp1, and vSGLT.
Run the Modeller 9.187 align tool to perform multiple sequence alignment overlapping the crystal structures of the templates.
Remove the putative sequences of NIS transmembrane helices 1, 12, and 13; keep residues 50‑439 (the 5+5 fold).
Align the remaining NIS residues with the 5+5 folds of the six templates.
Model NIS TM 1 and TM 12 using vSGLT TM 1 (PDB 2XQ2) and TM 12 (PDB 3DH4) as references.
Exclude TM 13 from modeling because of poor sequence identity with all templates.

steps.title: Generate NIS 3D models with constraints
steps.instruction: Build three NIS models (vSGLT‑like, LeuT‑like, mixed) with Modeller 9.187 automodel, imposing α‑helical constraints on residues 85‑99, 279‑296, 393‑401, 409‑425, and 428‑438; for each model generate 500 structures, evaluate them with pdfpdb7, DOPE9 and GA34110 scores, and retain 5‑10 structures with the lowest DOPE and highest GA341 scores for further processing.

substeps.instruction: Divide the six templates into two groups: vSGLT‑like (vSGLT, Mhp1) and LeuT‑like (LeuT, AdiC, BetP, dDAT).
Create three comparative models of NIS: a vSGLT‑like model, a LeuT‑like model, and a mixed model using all six templates.
Use the automodel function in Modeller 9.187, applying α‑helical constraints to residues 85‑99, 279‑296, 393‑401, 409‑425, and 428‑438.
For each model, generate 500 independent structures.
Assess each structure with the pdfpdb7, DOPE9, and GA34110 scoring functions.
Select 5‑10 structures per model that have the lowest DOPE scores and the highest GA341 scores; overlap these with the templates to inspect backbone geometry and key residues.
Pass the selected structures to the next step for side‑chain relaxation.

steps.title: Relax side chains in implicit membrane
steps.instruction: Subject the selected NIS structures to side‑chain relaxation using ROSETTA MP protocols in an implicit membrane environment, after manually preparing membrane span files based on the initial 3D models.

substeps.instruction: Manually create ROSETTA span files that define the membrane topology using the initial NIS 3D structures as a reference.
Run the ROSETTA MP side‑chain relaxation protocol with an implicit membrane model on each selected NIS structure.

steps.title: Create decoys, score, cluster, select representative
steps.instruction: For each of the three relaxed NIS models generate 2000 decoy structures with ROSETTA, score them using mpframework_smooth_fa_2012, cluster the scored decoys, and choose the center of the largest lowest‑energy cluster as the final representative model for subsequent GCMC and MD simulations.

substeps.instruction: Generate 2000 decoy structures per NIS model using ROSETTA.
Score all decoys with the mpframework_smooth_fa_2012 scoring function.
Cluster the scored decoys using the ROSETTA cluster tool.
Identify the largest cluster with the lowest energy and select its centroid as the representative NIS model for downstream GCMC and molecular dynamics simulations.
